correctness.rationale: Gaussian orthogonality implies independent normalized chi-squared column norms. Conditional gamma integration gives the exact full pivot probability; an integer-gamma CDF expansion gives the even-row finite sum. Beta endpoint Laplace asymptotics give the individual exponential rate and prefactor; a strict two-runner Chernoff-rate comparison and non-runner beta-rate separation prove the exact runner-up multiplicity. The O(loglog) row-count correction follows by asymptotic inversion. The embedded verifier passed 80 finite checks; the proof does not rely on stochastic experiments.

A pairwise tail upper bound alone cannot establish the asymptotically exact number of tied runners-up because all pairwise events share one random denominator; the supplied strict two-event exponent resolves this dependence. The inspected primary claims do not subsume that leading constant or the full finite sum.

value.rationale: The benchmark isolates sketch-induced pivot errors on a natural orthogonal-column matrix family, yields an exact computable finite-sketch calibration for multiple candidates, and proves that the sharp failure rate depends only on the strongest runner-up squared norm and its multiplicity despite shared-denominator dependence. It quantifies sketch dimension for a target risk down to the logarithmic correction, materially refining generic all-column union-bound calibration without claiming a new general QR factorization error theorem.
